issues.description: Unbounded log buffer can cause OOM during long crash loops or pre-connect hangs
issues.detail: _BufferingHandler in telemetry/traces.py keeps every LogRecord in self.buffer with no size cap, no time window, and no eviction. If the job entry hangs or loops before init_recording is called (which is the exact crash scenario this PR targets), memory will grow without bound. A bounded deque (e.g. collections.deque(maxlen=N)) or a byte/size cap is needed since the whole point is to capture crashy long-tail scenarios.

issues.description: Removing OTLP LoggingHandler from root logger in _shutdown_telemetry mutates global logging state for the whole process
issues.detail: _shutdown_telemetry() in traces.py iterates root.handlers and removes every LoggingHandler instance. In a worker process that runs multiple jobs or shares a process-wide root logger, this removes handlers that belong to other tracer/logger providers and silently breaks log forwarding for subsequent jobs. The handler removal should be scoped to the specific LoggerProvider being shut down, not done by isinstance check on the root logger.

issues.description: Race between setting _shutdown_fut on entry-task failure and the connect path setting it elsewhere
issues.detail: _on_entry_done in job_proc_lazy_main.py now force-resolves self._shutdown_fut with InvalidStateError suppression. This is fine for the crash case, but it also fires when the task raised AFTER connect()/shutdown() ran normally (where shutdown_fut may already be set with a different reason). The suppress hides that; the result is that legitimate shutdown reasons can be silently shadowed by 'job crashed' if ordering flips. Consider guarding with `if not self._shutdown_fut.done()` and explicitly logging when we override.

issues.description: _on_cleanup re-enters init_recording even when the user explicitly opted out of recording
issues.detail: In job.py _on_cleanup, if _early_log_handler is not None and recording was not initialized, the code unconditionally calls init_recording with logs=True. _start_log_buffering already checks enable_recording and is_cloud, so the handler is only created when the server wants recording — but the user may have called init_recording(RecordingOptions(logs=False)) and that path returns early via the new _stop_log_buffering branch BEFORE setting _recording_initialized=True. That early-return at line 645-647 means subsequent calls re-enter the full init path. The control flow around init_recording's two early-returns (the new stop branch vs the original) needs a comment or refactor to make precedence explicit.

issues.description: init_recording behavior change: _stop_log_buffering now fires on every early-return, including the 'already initialized' path
issues.detail: Previously the early return at `if self._recording_initialized or not is_cloud(self._info.url): return` was a pure no-op. Now it always calls _stop_log_buffering(). If init_recording is called multiple times (idempotent guard) and any caller relies on the buffer still being active until the first successful init, this changes semantics. More importantly, if is_cloud() is False but a buffer somehow exists (shouldn't, but defense in depth), we'd drop it silently. Worth an explicit comment that 'reaching this branch means we won't be uploading, so drop the buffer'.

issues.description: _flush_early_log_buffer relies on first LoggingHandler in root.handlers being the OTLP one just installed
issues.detail: The code does `for h in root.handlers: if isinstance(h, LoggingHandler): ... break`. If any other code path has already installed an OTLP LoggingHandler (e.g. from a previous job in the same process, or a user-side OpenTelemetry setup), the replay goes to the wrong handler. Capture the handler reference at _setup_cloud_tracer time and pass it in explicitly rather than discovering by isinstance.

issues.description: Disabling pytest-xdist (-n auto) removed and test_plugin_google_stt.py dropped without explanation
issues.detail: makefile change removes parallel test execution and silently drops test_plugin_google_stt.py from the unit-tests target. The PR description is about log upload on crash; these test changes look like an unrelated workaround for flaky tests. They need a comment in the diff explaining why (likely IPC pool tests racing under xdist) or a separate PR. Removing a test file from CI is a P1 in any review.

issues.description: Reordering in worker.py _on_accept: pending_assignments registered after queue_msg vs before
issues.detail: The diff moves `self._pending_assignments[job_req.id] = wait_assignment` to BEFORE `await self._queue_msg(availability_resp)`. This is actually a fix — it eliminates the race where the server sends the assignment before we register the future — but it's bundled into an unrelated PR with no test and no commit message tie-in. Worth calling out: this is a correctness fix that deserves its own line in the PR description so reviewers know to look for it.

issues.description: Replayed log records carry original timestamps but are emitted at flush time — downstream may misorder them
issues.detail: _flush_early_log_buffer calls h.emit(record) on stored LogRecord objects. The records keep their original `created` timestamps, but OTLP LogRecordProcessor batches by emit-call time. Downstream log viewers ordered by ingestion time will show crash logs out of order relative to logs emitted after init_recording. Either set record.created to now() with a 'replayed_at' attribute, or document the expected timestamp semantics.

issues.description: _BufferingHandler captures records on the root logger with no level filter; will buffer DEBUG and noisy library logs
issues.detail: logging.Handler default level is NOTSET (0), so _BufferingHandler accepts every record that reaches root. In a crash scenario with verbose libraries (asyncio, urllib3, opentelemetry itself) the buffer fills with noise that competes with actual crash signal. Set a sensible default (INFO or WARNING) or accept the existing root level only.

issues.description: broad `except Exception` in _on_cleanup swallows the original error
issues.detail: The new init_recording attempt in _on_cleanup wraps the call in `except Exception` and only logs. That's reasonable for a best-effort crash path, but `logger.exception` here writes to handlers that include the buffering handler we just decided to drop. Slight log-loop risk; consider logging via a plain stderr fallback.

issues.description: RecordingOptions imported lazily inside _on_cleanup creates a circular-import hint
issues.detail: The local `from .voice.agent_session import RecordingOptions` inside _on_cleanup suggests a circular import between job.py and voice/agent_session.py. This works but is fragile; consider moving RecordingOptions to a leaf module (e.g. a types module) so it can be imported at module top.

issues.description: new emit('process_closed', proc) in proc_pool may surprise existing listeners with a not-yet-fully-initialized proc
issues.detail: proc_pool.py now emits process_closed when initialization fails. Existing listeners may have assumed process_closed only fires after a successful init. The test was updated to handle proc.pid being None, which suggests this is a real behavior change. Worth a one-line note in the event's docstring that it can now fire for failed-init procs.
Two methods say 'log_buffering', one says 'early_log_buffer'. Pick one. Also _early_log_handler vs the methods using 'log_buffer' is inconsistent.

issues.description: pyproject.toml adds pythonpath=['.'] which may shadow installed packages during tests
issues.detail: Adding `pythonpath = ['.']` under [tool.pytest.ini_options] makes pytest prepend the repo root to sys.path. Combined with the makefile change removing PYTHONPATH=$PWD, this is the intended replacement — but it now applies to every pytest invocation, not just the make target. If there are top-level directories that shadow installed package names this could cause import surprises.

dissents.topic: Should the buffer be bounded, or is unboundedness acceptable for a crash-only path?

positions.position: Unbounded buffer is unacceptable: a tight crash loop with verbose logging will OOM the worker before any logs can be uploaded, defeating the feature's purpose. Must be a bounded deque.
Real crashes happen within seconds and produce hundreds of records, not millions. A bound can be added in a follow-up; shipping the visibility fix today unblocks production debugging.

dissents.topic: Is removing OTLP LoggingHandlers in _shutdown_telemetry by isinstance scan safe?

positions.position: Wrong — it conflates 'a LoggingHandler' with 'the LoggingHandler tied to this LoggerProvider'. Multi-tenant or nested telemetry setups will break. Track the handler reference at install time.

In this codebase only one LoggerProvider is ever installed per process and only one LoggingHandler exists. The scan is fine for the actual deployment pattern; over-engineering it adds plumbing for a hypothetical.

dissents.topic: Should the bundled changes (makefile, worker.py reorder, pyproject pythonpath, test changes) be in this PR?

positions.position: No — they're unrelated to log upload and the worker.py reorder is a separate race fix that needs its own review and changelog entry.

Yes — the IPC test changes and makefile/pyproject changes are likely needed to make the new flush logic testable, and the worker reorder might have been discovered while debugging the same crash. Bundling is fine if reviewer attention is drawn to each piece.

set_result inside the done callback with suppress(InvalidStateError) is correct only if no other code path expects a specific reason. The suppress hides ordering bugs and should at minimum log when it fires.
It's the right primitive for the job — a future that resolves once, no matter who gets there first. The suppress is idiomatic for 'I might not be the first writer.'

review.summary: The PR's core idea — buffer logs early, replay them through OTLP once recording initializes, and force-flush on crash — is sound and addresses a real observability gap. However, the buffering implementation has two P0 problems: the buffer is unbounded (defeating the crash-path purpose under loops or hangs), and _shutdown_telemetry mutates global root-logger state by removing handlers via isinstance scan rather than tracking the specific handler it installed. Several P1 concerns cluster around fragile handler discovery by isinstance, silent semantic changes to init_recording's early-return paths, replayed-record timestamp ordering, and a force-resolve of _shutdown_fut that can shadow legitimate shutdown reasons. The PR also bundles unrelated changes (makefile parallel-test removal, dropped test file, worker.py assignment-registration reorder, pyproject pythonpath) that should be called out explicitly or split out. Fix the unbounded buffer and the global handler-removal scoping before merge; the rest can be addressed in follow-up if the team accepts the pragmatic-shipper framing for the bundled changes.
